```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r attach}
library(priogridR)
```

The temporal utilities operate within PRIO-GRID cells, order observations by
an explicit time column, and return rows in their original order. Optional
grouping columns can separate scenarios, sources, or other repeated panels.

```{r data}
config <- priogrid::pg_config(nrow = 2, ncol = 3, verbose = FALSE)

panel <- data.frame(
  pgid = rep(1:2, each = 5),
  year = rep(2018:2022, 2),
  events = c(0, 1, 3, 0, 2, 5, 4, 6, 8, 7),
  onset = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE,
            FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)
)
```

## Lags and leads

`pg_temporal_lag()` and `pg_temporal_lead()` shift observations only within
the same cell. The first lag and final lead in each cell are therefore
missing.

```{r shifts}
lagged <- pg_temporal_lag(
  panel, value = "events", time = "year", config = config
)

shifted <- pg_temporal_lead(
  lagged, value = "events", time = "year", config = config
)

shifted[c("pgid", "year", "events", "events_lag1", "events_lead1")]
```

Set `periods` to a positive integer for longer shifts. Use `group` when a cell
contains several independent sequences, such as alternative scenarios.

## Changes

`pg_temporal_change()` provides ordinary differences, percentage changes, and
log differences. Percentage changes are missing when the earlier value is
zero. Log differences are missing unless both values are strictly positive.

```{r changes}
pg_temporal_change(
  panel,
  value = "events",
  time = "year",
  type = "difference",
  config = config
)[c("pgid", "year", "events", "events_difference")]
```

## Rolling summaries

Rolling windows may be trailing (`"right"`), centered, or forward
(`"left"`). `min_obs` controls how many non-missing values are required, while
`na_rm` determines whether missing values invalidate an otherwise sufficiently
populated window.

```{r rolling}
rolled <- pg_rolling_summary(
  panel,
  value = "events",
  time = "year",
  window = 3,
  fun = "mean",
  align = "right",
  min_obs = 2,
  na_rm = TRUE,
  config = config
)

rolled[c("pgid", "year", "events", "events_rolling_mean_3")]
```

## Time since an event

`pg_time_since()` resets to zero whenever an event occurs. Rows before the
first event in each cell remain missing.

```{r time-since}
elapsed <- pg_time_since(
  panel,
  event = "onset",
  time = "year",
  units = "periods",
  config = config
)

elapsed[c("pgid", "year", "onset", "onset_time_since")]
```

For irregularly spaced `Date` or `POSIXt` observations, use `units = "days"`
to calculate elapsed calendar days.

## Row-based versus calendar-complete periods

Shifts and rolling windows are deliberately row based. If a cell has records
for 2018 and 2020 but not 2019, its one-row lag treats 2018 as the previous
observation. This avoids silently inventing observations or choosing values
for structural gaps.

When a lag or window must correspond to consecutive configured periods,
complete the panel first:

```{r complete}
incomplete <- panel[!(panel$pgid == 1 & panel$year == 2020), ]

complete <- pg_complete_panel(
  incomplete,
  time = "year",
  cells = 1:2,
  times = 2018:2022,
  config = config
)

pg_temporal_lag(
  complete, value = "events", time = "year", config = config
)
```

The introduced row retains a missing value unless a substantively justified
fill rule is supplied to `pg_complete_panel()`.
